artifacts.summary: Maps all five README-restructure acceptance items to exact line numbers and destination sections, verifies the item-1 40-line budget is currently at zero slack, confirms the saturation-footnote aside is already recorded in docs/reference/paper-definitions-of-record.md (deletion not migration), confirms C15 anchor citations survive the two paragraph deletions, and confirms both check-module-invariants.sh --no-build and readme-lint.sh are green at baseline.

memory_candidates.content: In this repo, scripts/readme-lint.sh's default (CI) invocation scopes to root FormalSystem only, so it does NOT check root README.md's own markdown links/paths. That coverage is actually provided by check-module-invariants.sh's C12 (slash-shaped source paths) and C13 (relative markdown links), both scoped to docs/ + README.md. When a task's acceptance criteria say 'readme-lint.sh green' for a root-README edit, also verify C12/C13 explicitly rather than assuming readme-lint.sh alone covers it.

check-module-invariants.sh's C14 stale-axiom-count regex operates per source line, not per paragraph. README.md:274-275 currently contains the phrase 'the 45 TM schemata' split across a line break, which is why it does not trip C14's digit-then-word stale-count pattern despite '45' being a tracked figure. Any prose reflow/reformatting near that text should preserve the line break or reword it, or C14 will fail for a reason unrelated to the edit being made.

docs/reference/paper-definitions-of-record.md has an established pattern for prose-only additions that require no anchor pin or re-hash: a dated section explicitly marked 'permanent, prose only, no re-pin' (e.g. 'Language correspondence (2026-09-08)'), or a short 'Note:' appended directly to an existing per-anchor entry (e.g. def:frame-properties's 'Note: promoted into coverage by this task'). Use one of these two shapes rather than inventing a new structure when adding narrative that doesn't touch the paper-anchor MANIFEST.
